premises: Aluminum has relatively higher diffusivity in the BCC matrix at intermediate temperatures (1350–1100 °C)
Differential elemental diffusion during cooling can cause local aluminum segregation
Local aluminum segregation destabilizes BCC and triggers nucleation of secondary phases (FCC/sigma)
Slow cooling or dwells in the critical window allow this segregation, while rapid quenching suppresses it
